chapter: Joining Goodman and views on arranging
title: Sondheim, orchestrators and composers
summary: He distinguishes composers from tunesmiths and the orchestrator's low standing.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: One of the few musicals I heard that really was an exception of that, was Sweeney Todd.
You mentioned that the other day.

I heard A Little Night Music was that way too. I think you have to give Sondheim his due, and I never know how much goes to the orchestrator and how much goes to composer. It depends really on the guy who does--I use that word advisedly, because most Broadway writers are not composers; they're tunesmiths. There is a huge difference. But Sondheim, not having worked with him, I really don't know. I have a suspicion that he watches his notes carefully.

I worked with people like that; Robert Emmet Dolling was one, and he translated his setting, he made his--even their orchestral settings--we were talking about this sort of thing before, about Hollywood,

how people would give a melody line and they would work it out according to the film. They'll give a breakdown of the film and say you do it. That guy then is the composer, the guy who gave the notes, although he is not composing at all. It's being an executor.

It's hard to tell on a Broadway musical in any case, if it comes out being a unified affair, someone had to make sure that it did that and that person has to have power. It can be the producer, it can be the director or the guy that wrote the tunes, but certainly never the orchestrator; he doesn't have that kind of power. He's the low man on the totem pole.

There's only one person lower than an orchestrator in a Broadway musical, and that's they guys who play in the band, the pit. The whole essence of a Broadway musical, to me, is a combination of soap opera and vaudeville, and in both cases
Music is being used as a secondary function.
No matter whether you're doing a Broadway show or a movie score.
That's right, and how many people misconstrue the purpose. Unfortunately for music, it can't defend itself either.
Just for the record, what are some of the--do you want to talk about the names of some of the shows you've scored, or would you rather pass?
